title: Renewal Risk Heatmap & High-touch Intake Routing for Strategic Accounts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem: Major strategic accounts (top 50 by ARR) have opaque renewal risk signals. CS teams receive ad-hoc escalations near renewal windows with inconsistent prioritization. Product and GTM are missing an operationalized, consistent intake so roadmap inputs from top customers are handled predictably and routed to the correct team with measurable SLAs.

Goal: Build a renewal-risk heatmap and high-touch intake routing layer that surfaces prioritized accounts to PM/CS/Eng triage, creates standardized playbooks for common renewal blockers, and feeds prioritized asks into the quarterly roadmap/early-access lanes. This will (1) reduce last-minute escalations, (2) improve renewal conversation preparedness, and (3) increase conversion/renewal NRR for prioritized accounts.

Scope:
- Productize a Renewal Risk Heatmap: combine signals (ARR, renewal date, product usage drop, error rates from Console, support severity, NPS, recent escalations, legal/contract concerns). Heatmap lives in Console + CS dashboard.
- High-touch Intake Routing: automated routing rules that push accounts into three lanes: "Immediate Triage" (CS + PM + Solutions Eng), "Quarterly Roadmap Candidate" (PM backlog with SLAs), "Low Priority / Monitor".
- Playbook templates: engineering mitigation steps, temporary feature toggles, proposed compensation frameworks, dedicated escalation contact list.
- Integration points: SFDC (renewal dates/opportunities), Zendesk/Jira for support incidents, Redwood Console usage metrics, internal churn model scores from Research.
- Outputs to roadmap: standardized intake tickets (PM backlog format) with required fields and priority score; weekly triage cadence and decision log.

Out of scope for this ticket: billing/contract negotiation workflows (Finance lead), automated pricing adjustments, or a full churn prediction model retrain. This ticket focuses on the operational intake, visualization, and routing logic for strategic accounts.
acceptance_criteria: Heatmap prototype available in Console and CS dashboard showing top 50 accounts with composite risk score and contributing signals
Routing rules defined and implemented in the intake service so accounts are auto-assigned to one of three lanes with audit trail
Playbook templates (technical, commercial, and legal checklists) exist in Confluence and are linked from intake tickets
Weekly triage workflow established with documented SLAs and a decision log accessible to PM/CS/Eng
At least two pilot accounts processed end-to-end through the new intake + playbook flow and retrospective notes captured
success_metrics: Reduce number of renewal escalations happening within 14 days of renewal by 50% for pilot accounts
Increase renewal close rate for top 50 accounts by 10 percentage points in the following quarter
Mean time from escalation to triage assignment is < 4 hours
Percent of intake tickets with complete required fields >= 90%
proposed_timeline: Week 1 (2026-02-22 to 2026-02-28): Data discovery, final signal list, prototype wireframes
Week 2: Heatmap MVP implemented in internal Console, routing rule design and contract with CS team
Week 3: Playbooks drafted, intake automation hooked to SFDC/Zendesk, pilot rollouts with 2 accounts
Week 4: Retrospective, iterate on scoring, finalize SLA and handbook, roadmap integration for Q2 cadence
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Signal quality (missing or noisy usage metrics) - Mitigation: fallback weighting that prefers deterministic signals (renewal date, support severity) until usage metrics stabilize
Risk: Cross-team SLAs not honored - Mitigation: formalize weekly triage meeting and exec sponsor with CS leadership
Risk: Too many accounts marked 'high' flooding triage - Mitigation: calibrate score thresholds for pilot and add a capacity flag to intake
Risk: Legal/commercial edge cases - Mitigation: include legal reviewer in triage for any ticket that includes 'contract' or 'credit' labels
